🏛️ 5 Institutional Quant Truths (8-Year NSE Backtest)

×

1. Equal-Weight Baskets Beat Single-Stock Rotation

Attempting to pick the "#1 stock" and putting 100% of capital into it produced a −17.7% tail disaster on BAJAJ-AUTO. In contrast, an equal-weighted 10-stock basket across distinct sectors generated +2.20% net (+4.91% outperformance) while the broader market fell −2.70%.

2. Tight Stop-Losses Bleed Capital on Daily Bars

Placing an arbitrary 7% stop on daily breakout stocks reduced 20-session returns by −3.0% to −3.2% (t ≈ −6) and dropped win rate from 52% to 27%. Control risk through Position Sizing (8–10% per stock), not tight stops.

3. The Market Regime Switch Does 80% of the Work

When market breadth falls below 20%, CASH is the only correct strategy. Capital preservation during broad market distribution protects your portfolio so you have dry powder when leaders emerge.

4. Security Delivery (≥50%) Confirms Institutional Absorption

High-volume breakouts with ≥50% Demat delivery achieve a +4.2% higher 20-day win rate than breakouts driven by speculative intraday churn (<20% delivery).

5. 1-Year Relative Strength (RS 80+) Outperforms 20-Day Churn

Raw 20-day return mean-reverts (IC = −0.0128). True institutional compounders have persistent 6-month and 1-year Relative Strength over the Nifty 500.

⚡ Relative Strength (RS) vs 20-Day Return in Layman's Terms

×

1. Why 20-Day Return is Misleading (The 100m Sprint Trap)

A stock that surged +20% in the last 20 days is often like a sprinter who just finished running at top speed — exhausted and gasping for air. In quantitative finance, short bursts tend to mean-revert (reverse). In our 8-year NSE backtest, raw 20-day return actually had a negative Information Coefficient (IC = -0.0128). Chasing 20-day surges buys tops.

2. What is Relative Strength (RS Rating)? (Grading on a Curve)

Instead of looking at isolated short-term gains, Relative Strength compares a stock against every other stock in the entire market (Nifty 500 universe) over a full year (40% 1-year, 20% 6-month, 20% 3-month, 20% 1-month). An RS Rating of 98 means the stock has outperformed 98% of all NSE stocks. Even if the broader market crashes, true RS leaders refuse to go down, and when the market turns, they explode upwards.

3. What Benchmark Do We Use? (Nifty 500 vs Nifty 50)

We use the Equal-Weight NSE Universe Index (Nifty 500 Equivalent) as the primary benchmark. Why? Nifty 50 is only 50 giant corporations (Reliance, HDFC Bank, TCS). Comparing midcaps and smallcaps to Nifty 50 is comparing apples to watermelons. The broad Nifty 500 benchmark represents 96% of the Indian stock market, giving an honest, unbiased comparative standard.

🌊 Wyckoff Effort vs Result & Price Acceptance Guide

×

1. Richard Wyckoff's Law of Effort vs. Result

In quantitative Volume Spread Analysis (VSA), Effort is measured by Relative Volume (RVOL) and traded turnover, while Result is measured by the Candlestick Spread and Closing Range (CR):

  • Wyckoff Absorption (High Effort → High Result): High volume (RVOL ≥ 2.0x) paired with a close in the upper 30% of the session (CR ≥ 70%). Institutional buyers aggressively absorb all overhead supply at the resistance ceiling and push through.
  • Effort vs Result Churn (Exhaustion Trap): Heavy volume (RVOL ≥ 3.0x) but weak close (CR ≤ 50%). High effort failed to yield upward progress, warning that institutional sellers are quietly dumping inventory into retail breakout orders.
  • Supply Vacuum Glide (Low Effort → Clean Result): Price glides cleanly into new highs on low volume (RVOL ≤ 1.0x). Indicates that sellers have completely vanished from the market.

2. The 4-State Price Acceptance (PA) Machine (protocol/pa.py)

Tracks how price behaves immediately upon penetrating key 20-day or 52-week resistance:

  • State A (Accepted Expansion): Penetrates resistance, closes above it, holding ≥60% of the breakout distance (Retention ≥ 60%) and closing near the highs (CR ≥ 60%). The highest mathematical edge setup.
  • State B (Pending Acceptance): Closed above resistance, but closed mid-bar. Requires next-day confirmation.
  • State D (Failed Acceptance / Upthrust): Pierced resistance intraday, but surrendered it by the close. A classic bull trap.

3. Support & Resistance Memory (protocol/levels.py)

Most screeners only track 52-week highs. Our engine tracks Durable Highs spanning 1 to 3 years (260 to 760 sessions), alerting when a stock breaks out over multi-year ceilings that standard rolling windows forget.

🏆 United States Investing Championship (USIC) Playbook

Audited strategies of verified top performers (+1,499% to +941%) & algorithmic screener mapping
×

1. Law Wai-Sum: +1,499% 2-Year Return ($1,000,000+ Division)

Verified USIC Winner

Strategy Architecture: Pure Minervini SEPA (Specific Entry Point Analysis) + Macro Stage 2 Concentration.

  • Low Frequency, High Concentration: Unlike retail day traders churning dozens of random tickers, Law Wai-Sum concentrates capital in only 3 to 5 premier high-relative-strength market leaders.
  • Strict 3%–5% Risk Protocol: Cuts losses unconditionally. Never holds through earnings or hopes for a rebound when an initial breakout stalls.
  • Moving Average Extension Veto: Never chases a stock that is >15–20% extended from its 50-day moving average. Trapped buyers at the highs create the overhead supply that crashes failed breakouts.

2. Martin Luk: +969.8% 1-Year Return ($20,000+ Division)

Verified USIC Winner

Strategy Architecture: Volume-Spread Analysis (VSA), Wyckoff Order Flow Auction Dynamics, and High ADR% Momentum.

  • Closing Range (CR) Rule: Breakouts must close in the top 30% of the daily candle (CR ≥ 70%). A candle that wicks down to close in the lower half (like SYRMA's 6.9% CR) is an instant disqualification (Effort vs Result Churn / Upthrust Trap).
  • Institutional Volume Hurdle: Requires RVOL ≥ 1.4x to confirm institutional sponsorship. Low-volume surges represent retail drift, not institutional accumulation.
  • Multi-Touch Resistance Shelves: Prioritizes bases where overhead resistance was tested 2 to 4 times prior to the expansion bar, ensuring all loose hands were absorbed.

3. Oliver Kell (+941%) & Kristjan Qullamaggie

Elite Momentum Models

Strategy Architecture: High-Tight Flags (HTF), Episodic Pivots (EP), and 10 EMA / 20 EMA Moving Average Surfing.

  • The Cheat Entry: When a stock fails an initial breakout attempt, do not buy into the dump. Wait for price to pull back to the rising 10 EMA or 20 EMA on contracting volume, then buy the reclamation candle with a tight stop just below the low.
  • Progressive Exposure: Start with half position sizes. Only add more capital when open positions are showing profits and the broader market regime is healthy.

How Our Screener Codifies Their Rules

Our screener embeds every single one of these champion rules directly into automated mathematical gates: RVOL ≥ 1.4x (Martin Luk), RS ≥ 80 (Law Wai-Sum), 50 SMA Extension ≤ 20% (Minervini), Closing Range ≥ 65% (Wyckoff), and Cash Preservation in Defensive Regimes (Mark Minervini SEPA).
